name: en-launch-review
transcript: [00:02] Priya: Okay, let's get going, I only have until half past.
[00:09] Priya: Right, the launch is currently set for the fifteenth of March, and QA says
[00:16] Priya: they need two more weeks on the payment flow.
[00:21] Lee: Two weeks is optimistic. Last time it took three.
[00:28] Dan: What if we ship without the Apple Pay part and add it later?
[00:34] Lee: That cuts maybe a third of the testing.
[00:39] Priya: Hmm, marketing already announced Apple Pay though.
[00:44] Dan: They announced it for the spring, not for day one.
[00:49] Priya: Fair. Okay so let's do that, launch on the fifteenth without Apple Pay, and Apple Pay follows in April.
[01:03] Priya: Dan, can you tell marketing today so they fix the banner?
[01:08] Dan: Yes, I'll message them this afternoon.
[01:13] Priya: And Lee, update the test plan so it only covers card payments, by Wednesday.
[01:23] Dan: Who is telling the partner at Northwind?
[01:27] Priya: Not sure yet, I'll think about it.
correct:
TITLE: Launch date and Apple Pay
SUMMARY: The team reviewed the launch schedule because QA needs more time on the payment flow. They agreed to launch on schedule without Apple Pay, which will follow later.
DECISION | ~00:49 | Launch stays on March 15 without Apple Pay; Apple Pay follows in April.
TASK | ~01:03 | Dan | today | Tell marketing to fix the banner that announces Apple Pay.
TASK | ~01:13 | Lee | Wednesday | Update the test plan to cover card payments only.
TOPIC: Testing time
POINT | QA asked for two more weeks on the payment flow, and Lee thinks it may take three.
POINT | Skipping Apple Pay cuts about a third of the testing.
OPEN | Nobody has been assigned to inform the partner at Northwind.
